title: Final size and early die-out of a stochastic SIR epidemic
ask: BENCHMARK. The protocol's grid has axes named `N` and `R0` and includes the setting N = 1000, R0 = 2.0. Declare a metric with id `final_fraction` (kind mean; one value per outbreak: the fraction of the population ever infected) and a metric with id `died_out_early` (kind proportion; one value per outbreak: 1 when fewer than 10 people were ever infected, else 0).

answers.source: (1 - 1/R0) z with z = 1 - exp(-R0 z) (Kermack-McKendrick 1927; branching-process die-out 1/R0) gives 0.3984; the benchmark's reference simulation of the same Markov model, 20000 outbreaks, gives 0.3978 (dev/evaluation/bench/reference.py::q4_sir)
min(1, 1/R0) = 0.5 for a branching process; the reference simulation with the 10-case cutoff gives 0.490
